title: Design Snake and Ladder
relevance: High — the canonical Flipkart/Uber-style machine-coding starter (campus + SDE-1/2); also a common OOD whiteboard warm-up. Tests OOP modeling, turn loops, Strategy/Builder, and (optionally) concurrent game sessions.
company_notes: Extremely common campus/machine-coding first LLD at Flipkart, Uber, Swiggy, Amazon new-grad and Indian product cos (timed CLI ~90–120 min via workat.tech). SDE-2 adds Strategy, chaining edges, concurrent sessions, RNG testability. FAANG OOD whiteboard is lighter coding, heavier clarifying Qs and class model. Among the top machine-coding LLD problems with parking lot, Splitwise, and Tic-Tac-Toe.

phases.goal: Lock mandatory FR/NFR, clarifying questions, and stated assumptions before any coding.

must_hit.point: Mandatory path: read snakes/ladders/players from CLI or file; fair d6 turns; print each move and the winner; start at 0; exact reach 100; overshoot stays put; apply snakes/ladders with chaining.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Candidate lists exact-land-on-100, overshoot=stay, start at 0, print moves/winner, and chaining as the workat happy path.

must_hit.point: Clarify extensions before coding: multi-dice, custom board size, extra turn on 6, cancel after 3 consecutive sixes, play until one left, whether same cell is allowed for multiple players.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Asks about multi-dice, board size, extra turn on 6 / 3 sixes, continue-until-last, and co-located players instead of assuming defaults.

must_hit.point: State assumptions: unique jump starts; no snake on final cell; no infinite jump cycles; at least 2 players; same cell OK unless product says capture.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Explicitly calls out unique starts, no snake at 100, no infinite cycles, ≥2 players, and same-cell allowed.

must_hit.point: Out of scope until asked: UI, persistence, online multiplayer networking, AI bots.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names UI/persistence/networking/bots as deferred and stays on core loop first.

probes: What must be true for a player to win, and what happens if the roll would go past the last cell?
Which optional rules will you support now versus defer?

hints.1: Start from the workat mandatory path before optional rules.
hints.2: Separate exact-win + chaining + print format from multi-dice / extra-turn / continue-until-last.
hints.3: Mandatory: start 0, exact 100, overshoot stay, chain jumps, print moves and winner; ask about 6 / 3 sixes / board size next.

phases.goal: Name the core domain objects and how jumps and turns are represented.

must_hit.point: Core entities: Board (size + jump map), Player (name, position), Dice (roll), Snake/Ladder or unified Jump/BoardEntity, Game or SnakeAndLadderService (turn loop + win).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Lists Board, Player, Dice, Snake/Ladder or Jump, and Game/Service without collapsing them into one god object.

must_hit.point: Prefer one Map from start to end (or destinations array) so landing resolves in O(1); inheritance is for validation, not per-move list scans.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says jump lookup is a map/array keyed by start cell, not scanning snake and ladder lists each move.

must_hit.point: Snake and ladder can share one Jump abstraction when behavior is identical; data (start/end direction) differs, not move logic.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Unifies snake/ladder as Jump/BoardEntity and notes only validation differs (start>end vs start<end).

must_hit.point: Optional GameManager owns concurrent sessions; one game remains a single-threaded turn machine with GameStatus NOT_STARTED|RUNNING|FINISHED.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Mentions GameManager only for multi-session and GameStatus for lifecycle, not for single-game core.

probes: What objects do you need, and how do you represent snakes and ladders on the board?
Why not keep separate lists and search them on every move?

hints.1: Think Board, Player, Dice, jumps, and something that runs the turn loop.
hints.2: Board holds size plus a start→end jump structure; Game/Service owns the queue and win check.
hints.3: Map/array jump resolve is O(1); Snake/Ladder subclasses optional for validation; GameManager is optional for sessions.

phases.goal: Sketch classes, relationships, and the patterns interviewers expect to hear.

must_hit.point: Turn rotation is a Queue of players: poll, roll, move, and if not won offer back — scales to N players without index math.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Uses Queue poll/offer for round-robin instead of a manual index modulo.

must_hit.point: Builder constructs Game from board + players + dice; Facade entry is play() or startGame(); Strategy covers dice count, win condition, and extra-turn-on-6 policy.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Names Builder for construction, Facade for play/startGame, Strategy for pluggable dice/win/turn rules.

must_hit.point: SRP split: Driver does I/O only; Service/Game orchestrates; Board is pure position resolution; Dice is injectable/mockable randomness.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Draws Driver → Service/Game → Board/Dice boundaries and refuses a single god class.

must_hit.point: Singleton only for a multi-game GameManager if used; prefer DI — do not force State/Observer unless asked.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Limits Singleton to GameManager and says DI is preferred; skips State/Observer unless prompted.

probes: Walk me through your class diagram and which patterns you would use.
Where does the turn loop live versus jump resolution?

hints.1: Separate who builds the game, who plays turns, and who resolves cells.
hints.2: Queue for turns; Builder for Game wiring; Strategy for optional rules; Board owns the jump map.
hints.3: Game/Service Facade + Queue<Player> + Board jumps + Dice; Builder/Strategy for construction and rule knobs; Singleton only if GameManager.

phases.goal: Describe the turn algorithm, exact-win handling, and chain resolution correctly.

must_hit.point: Per turn: poll player → Dice.roll → tentative = pos + roll; if tentative > size stay; else pos = Board.resolve(tentative) with chain jumps; if pos == size win/remove, else enqueue (or re-turn on 6).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Narrates poll → roll → overshoot check → resolve/chain → win or enqueue in that order.

must_hit.point: Default exact-win: pos + roll > size skips the move; first to pos == size wins — state this early.
must_hit.evidence_hint: States stay-put on overshoot and win only on exact last cell.

must_hit.point: Chaining is mandatory in workat: after a jump, if landing is another head/start keep resolving until stable; detect cycles (no infinite loop, no snake at 100, unique starts).
must_hit.evidence_hint: Loops jump resolution until stable and mentions a cycle/visited guard under the usual assumptions.

must_hit.point: API surface: Dice.roll, Board.getFinalPosition(pos), Game.play / startGame, takeTurn(Player); Driver only reads snakes, ladders, players and starts the game.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Sketches those method names and keeps parsing out of the service core.

probes: Trace one full turn when a player lands on a ladder that leads to a snake head.
What do you print and when does the game end on the mandatory path?

hints.1: Write the move as tentative position, then apply jumps, then check win.
hints.2: Overshoot leaves position unchanged; resolve may apply multiple jumps; queue rotates unless won.
hints.3: tentative>size → stay; else resolve with chain+cycle guard; pos==size → winner; else offer back to queue.

phases.goal: Show how optional rules plug in without rewriting the core turn loop.

must_hit.point: Hardcoded exact-win + single die passes mandatory; Strategy or flags win optional multi-dice, continue-until-last, and extra-turn follow-ups without rewriting startGame.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Keeps mandatory path simple and points optional rules at Strategy/setters rather than forking the loop.

must_hit.point: OCP/DIP signal: new win/dice/turn rules without editing the game loop; depend on Dice/strategy abstractions for testability.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says WinningStrategy/MovementStrategy (or equivalent) and injectable Dice so rules change at the edges.

must_hit.point: Extra turn on 6 is optional; three consecutive sixes often cancel the whole turn (return to turn-start position) — prefer a loop with consecutive-6 counter over recursion.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Describes optional re-roll on 6 and a consecutive-6 counter that can void the turn instead of recursive re-entry.

must_hit.point: Multi-dice and custom board size via noOfDices and boardSize params — do not hardcode 100 and 6 inside the loop.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Constructor/Builder knobs for dice count and board size; loop uses those values.

probes: How would you add extra turn on 6 and cancel after 3 sixes without rewriting play()?
Where would multi-dice and custom board size live?

hints.1: Treat optional rules as policies, not if-else sprawl in the middle of play.
hints.2: WinningStrategy / turn Strategy / setters on the service; Builder passes boardSize and dice count.
hints.3: Mandatory first; then Strategy for win/extra-turn; loop+counter for 3 sixes; noOfDices and boardSize instead of hardcoded 100/6.

phases.goal: Explain multi-session isolation and safe randomness without shared mutable game state.

must_hit.point: One game is single-threaded; multi-session means independent Game instances on separate threads — never share mutable board/player state across games.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Says each lobby gets its own Game/board/players; no cross-game shared cells.

must_hit.point: GameManager.startNewGame spawns independent games; synchronize only the manager’s game list, not board cells.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Locks or syncs the session registry only; each Game runs without board-level locking.

must_hit.point: Prefer ThreadLocalRandom or an injected RNG over a shared Random; inject a seed for deterministic tests.
must_hit.evidence_hint: Avoids one shared Random across threads and mentions injectable/seeded RNG for tests.

probes: How would you support many concurrent games safely?
What would you synchronize, and what must remain unshared?

hints.1: Think one game object per session, not one shared board.
hints.2: Manager tracks games; each Game is isolated on its own thread or executor task.
hints.3: startNewGame → new Game per thread; sync only the manager list; ThreadLocalRandom or injected RNG; no shared mutable board.

tradeoffs.topic: Separate Snake/Ladder classes vs unified Jump
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Separate classes encode validation (start > end vs start < end); unified Jump avoids duplicate lookup. Strong answer: one map for resolve plus optional subclasses for validation only.
Lists are fine for tiny boards; map/array is the expected clean answer and makes chaining trivial — avoid O(S+L) scans per move if claiming polish.
Hardcoding exact-win + single die passes the mandatory path; Strategy/flags win optional multi-dice / continue-until-last / extra-turn follow-ups without rewriting startGame.

tradeoffs.topic: Recursive roll-6-again vs loop with counters
tradeoffs.strong_answer: Recursion is short; a loop with a consecutive-6 counter is safer for the three-sixes-cancel rule.

gotchas.trap: Forgetting snake/ladder chaining when one jump lands on another head/start
gotchas.correction: In workat, keep resolving until stable and mention a cycle guard under no-infinite-loop assumptions.

gotchas.trap: Moving past 100 instead of staying put
gotchas.correction: Default interview rule is exact win: overshoot stays; bounce-back is an alternate WinningStrategy/movement rule.

gotchas.trap: Ignoring three consecutive sixes when offering extra turn on 6
gotchas.correction: Extra turn is optional; three consecutive often cancel the whole turn and return to turn-start position.

gotchas.trap: Assuming two players on the same cell is illegal
gotchas.correction: Usually allowed; no capture unless the product says otherwise.

gotchas.trap: Hardcoding board size 100 and die face 6 in the loop
gotchas.correction: Pass noOfDices and boardSize so multi-dice and custom boards do not require loop rewrites.

gotchas.trap: Sharing mutable board/player state across concurrent games
gotchas.correction: Independent Game per session; synchronize only the manager’s game list, not cells.

gotchas.trap: God-class that parses input, rolls dice, and prints in one file
gotchas.correction: Interviewers dock design score — split Driver I/O, service orchestration, and board jump map.

gotchas.trap: Finishing optional extensibility but failing mandatory move print / win
gotchas.correction: Ship the mandatory happy path first; optional Strategy/flags come after.
